title: Granite Switch 4.1: Chat, Decisions, and Speech from One Endpoint
gist: IBM announces Granite Switch 4.1 (8B and 30B), composing a general Decision aLoRA, a Guardian safety aLoRA and an embedded Granite Speech ASR model into one endpoint with roughly the base model's VRAM. IBM claims cache-sharing Activated LoRAs make adding specialist adapters nearly free versus Jev.

insights.claim: Granite Switch 4.1 8B and 30B bundle a general Decision aLoRA, a Guardian safety aLoRA and the Granite-Speech-5.0-Turbo-CTC ASR model with the base model in one model that uses about the same GPU VRAM as the base alone.
insights.speaker: Kate Soule
insights.so_what: More capabilities per GPU lowers serving cost for enterprise multi-task deployments.
insights.quote: That means more capabilities with fewer GPUs.

insights.claim: Because the adapters are Activated LoRAs, the KV cache from a base-model generation can be reused for later adapter decisions, and with IBM's vLLM contributions plus a co-located ASR encoder the model can switch between chat, decision and speech requests quickly.
insights.speaker: Kate Soule
insights.so_what: Cache reuse is the mechanism behind the claimed near-zero marginal cost of extra adapters; watch for independent latency tests.

insights.claim: IBM claims its Guardian aLoRA outperforms Jev 1.13, Microsoft-Decision-1, GPT-Luna-Decisions and Clef-Flash on average on safety-related decision tasks, and that Granite-Speech-5.0-Turbo-CTC is the fastest ASR model on the OpenASR Leaderboard; no numbers are given.
insights.speaker: Kate Soule
insights.so_what: Vendor claims without published figures; IBM says more data is coming in weeks.

insights.claim: IBM says specialized granitelib decision adapters can outperform generalist decision models like Jev on specialized classification tasks, and because adapters share the base KV cache, stacking specialists beside a generalist adds almost no cost.
insights.speaker: Kate Soule
insights.so_what: Argues for modular specialist adapters over single generalist decision models in enterprise classification.
insights.quote: adding specialists alongside a generalist decision adapter costs almost nothing
insights.locator: Granite Libraries: The OG Decision Models

insights.claim: In IBM's race, Granite-Switch-4.1-30B (frozen Granite base plus 4 specialized aLoRAs) finished a real-world 5-step RAG workflow much faster than Jev-27B (a frozen Qwen base plus 1 generic LoRA).
insights.speaker: Kate Soule
insights.so_what: Vendor-run comparison with no timings published; treat as directional.
insights.locator: Granite Libraries: The OG Decision Models

insights.claim: IBM plans an Adapter SDK for training adapters in Mellea and sees opportunity for community and third-party adapters, and a custom 3B Granite Switch model playing Doom reached 60 to 100 decisions per second versus Jev's reported 10, while also narrating.
insights.speaker: Kate Soule
insights.so_what: An adapter ecosystem could make Granite Switch a platform; the Doom figure compares against Jev's self-reported number.
insights.quote: Unlike Jev, this Granite Switch model can also narrate and respond to your questions while it is playing.
insights.locator: Compose and Extend Your Own Granite Switch Model
